summary: Full backend regression executed across /app/backend/tests/. When run in two batches (security/non-2FA suite, then test_two_factor.py and test_lockdown.py individually) ALL backend tests pass: 287+11+9 = 307 PASS, 0 product failures. Three stale-URL test failures in test_friends_hub_iteration21.py and test_shares_compare_iteration22.py were diagnosed as test-config drift (hardcoded preview URL `memory-recap-2026.preview.emergentagent.com`, current pod is `lockdown-command.preview.emergentagent.com`); overriding with `EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL=http://localhost:8001` makes them pass. test_moderation_iteration31.py had the same hardcoded URL and was patched to use env var (verified all 26 tests pass). The other 14 transient failures during the single-shot full run are caused by IP rate-limit (10 req/min on /api/auth/login in utils/rate_limit.py) being exhausted by per-class fixture re-logins — NOT product bugs; tests pass when grouped/spaced.

minor.issue: Aggressive 10 req/min per IP rate-limit on auth endpoints triggers cascading 429s when running the full pytest suite in one shot (multiple test files re-login per class). Not a product bug, but blocks CI single-shot runs. Consider a TEST-mode env flag or higher dev RPM, or share/cache login tokens across test classes.

rca of the issue: Two distinct test-infrastructure issues caused the only failures observed: (1) stale preview URL `memory-recap-2026.preview.emergentagent.com` hardcoded in 10 legacy test files — this pod is now `lockdown-command.preview.emergentagent.com`, so test fixtures insert seed rows into THIS pod's mongo while API calls hit the OTHER pod, returning 404 'Visit not found' / empty payloads. Mitigation: tests should read EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL from env or default to http://localhost:8001 (already applied to test_moderation_iteration31.py). (2) IP rate-limit of 10 req/min on /api/auth/login (utils/rate_limit.py) gets exhausted during full-suite runs because multiple test classes re-login on fixture setup; this manifests as 429 errors in test_lockdown.py and test_two_factor.py when they run AFTER other auth-heavy files. Mitigation: either bump dev RPM, exempt loopback IPs, or refactor tests to share a session-scoped login fixture. Neither is a product bug — Security Dashboard, 2FA, lockdown circuit-breaker, brute-force lockout, moderation gating, and super-admin tier mutation enforcement all verified WORKING.
